transcript.text: Samsung WD90T534DBW washer dryer - clothes are still damp at the end of the wash and dry programme. It's not that old. Is the heater going?

It is unlikely that the heating element (heater) has failed, especially if the machine is relatively new and the issue is specifically "damp" rather than "soaking wet." Here’s why, along with the most probable causes for your Samsung WD90T534DBW:

### Why It’s Probably Not the Heater
1.  If the heater were dead: The machine would still tumble and wash, but it would only dry using ambient air (like a fan-only cycle). Clothes would come out damp to wet, not just "slightly damp." They would also likely smell musty because moisture isn’t being evaporated.
2.  Dampness usually means: The cycle is ending too soon, heat isn’t being applied long enough, or airflow/moisture sensing is faulty.

---

### Most Likely Causes (in order of probability)

#### 1. Overloading the Machine ⚠️
• This is the #1 cause. The WD90T534DBW has a 9kg wash / 6kg dry capacity.
• If you put in more than 6kg of laundry for drying, or even a full 9kg load (which is heavy when wet), the dryer cannot circulate air properly through the dense mass of clothes.
• Fix: Reduce loads to no more than 5–6 kg for drying. Leave space so you can easily put your hand inside the drum.

#### 2. Clogged Condenser or Filters 🔧
Your machine is a condenser dryer. It needs:
• Lint filter(s): Check the small lint trap in the door seal and any larger filters at the bottom front (behind the kickplate). If these are clogged, airflow is restricted.
• Condenser unit: Located behind the lower front panel. If this is dirty, heat can’t dissipate properly, and moisture isn’t removed efficiently.
• Fix: Clean all filters monthly. Every 3–6 months, remove the condenser (usually two plastic fins) and rinse it under a shower until water runs clear.

#### 3. Moisture Sensor Issues 💧
Samsung dryers use humidity sensors to detect when clothes are dry. If these are dirty or faulty:
• The machine thinks clothes are still damp and stops prematurely, OR
• It over-dries (but you’re reporting under-drying).
• Fix: Locate the two metal strips inside the drum (usually on the right side). Wipe them with a damp cloth and mild detergent to remove fabric softener residue. Fabric softener coats sensors and makes them think clothes are dry when they’re not.

#### 4. Wrong Programme Selected 📋
• Some programmes (e.g., "Cotton," "Synthetic") have different end-dry settings. If you selected a programme with "Iron Dry" or "Extra Damp" setting, it will intentionally leave clothes damp for ironing.
• Fix: Check the display. Ensure you’re using a standard dry programme (e.g., "Cotton Dry" or "Auto Dry") and that no "damp" option is selected.

#### 5. Ventilation/Exhaust Issues 🌬️
• Even though it’s a condenser dryer, it still needs to expel hot, moist air from the top rear of the machine into the room. If the area around the exhaust vent is blocked or poorly ventilated, humidity builds up in the machine and reduces drying efficiency.
• Fix: Ensure there’s at least 10–15 cm of space behind and above the machine for airflow.

---

### Quick Diagnostic Test
To confirm if the heater is working:
1.  Run a "Quick Dry" or "Time Dry" programme (e.g., 30 minutes) with no clothes inside.
2.  After 5–10 minutes, carefully place your hand near the air outlet (top rear of the machine).
3.  If you feel hot air: The heater is working. The problem is airflow, load size, or sensors.
4.  If no heat comes out: The heater, thermostat, or control board may be faulty. Contact Samsung support.

---

### Recommended Action Plan
1.  Reduce load size to ≤6 kg for drying.
2.  Clean all filters (door seal lint trap + bottom condenser filter).
3.  Wipe the moisture sensors inside the drum with a damp cloth.
4.  Ensure proper ventilation around the machine.
5.  If problems persist, run the "No Clothes" heat test above to confirm heater function.

If the heater is confirmed working and all filters/sensors are clean, contact Samsung support for potential sensor or control board issues.

I load the full 9kg drum and do wash and dry in one go, and the manual says 6kg for drying. I also often turn the spin down to 800. Drum gets hot and clothes are warm but damp at the end, no error codes.

You have identified both major issues: overloading and under-spinning. These two factors combined are almost certainly why your clothes come out damp.

Here’s exactly what is happening and how to fix it:

### 1. The Overload Problem (9kg vs. 6kg)
When you put a full 9kg load into the dryer, the clothes form a dense "log" in the center of the drum. Air cannot circulate through the middle of this log. Even though the heater is working and the outside of the clothes are warm, the moisture trapped inside the dense bundle has nowhere to go. The machine stops because its sensors detect that the outside feels dry, while the inside remains wet.

### 2. The Spin Speed Problem (800 RPM)
This is likely your biggest culprit for dampness. A washer-dryer relies on high-speed spinning to remove as much water as possible before the drying cycle even begins.
• At 1400–1600 RPM: Most of the free water is forced out. The dryer only needs to evaporate the remaining moisture in the fibers.
• At 800 RPM: A significant amount of free water remains in the clothes. The dryer now has to spend much longer (and use more energy) just boiling off that extra water. Since the cycle time is fixed or sensor-based, it often runs out of time before all that excess moisture can be evaporated.

### How to Fix It
1.  Reduce Load Size: For drying, stick to the manual’s recommendation of 6kg max. If you have a large load, split it into two smaller loads for drying.
2.  Increase Spin Speed: Set your wash cycle to spin at 1400 RPM or higher (if fabric allows). This removes the bulk of the water before drying begins, making the drying process far more efficient and effective.
3.  Clean the Condenser & Filters: Even with correct loading, a dirty condenser will reduce efficiency. Clean the lint filters after every cycle and rinse the condenser unit monthly.

By reducing the load to 6kg and spinning at 1400+ RPM, you should see a dramatic improvement in dryness.
